review_candidates.title: Director Government Relations
review_candidates.description: Job Description HONEYWELL AEROSPACE Government Relations – Director, Japan (hybrid) THE OPPORTUNITY Honeywell Aerospace is seeking a Director of Government Relations, Japan, to lead engagement with the Japanese government, parliament, regulators, and key external stakeholders and serve as an expert guide within Honeywell Aerospace enabling business growth in Japan and the region. Based in Tokyo, this role will represent Honeywell Aerospace’s interests, guiding internal actions impacted by Japanese government policies and actions, while shaping external government community engagement across civil aviation, defense, industrial strategy, aviation safety and certification, tax and trade, sustainability, and emerging aerospace technologies to achieve optimal business outcomes. This position reports to the Senior Vice President, Global Government Relations, located in Washington, DC and aligns with our international GR team led from Brussels. The Director will serve as a senior strategic interface between Japanese government decision-makers and Honeywell Aerospace business leaders, ensuring alignment between public policy outcomes and the company’s operational, manufacturing, and technology priorities. A key responsibility is to drive a cohesive Japan government relations strategy and enable favorable business outcomes by building strong relationships personally and for company leaders across national and local governments, including relative to government bilateral relations with important counterparts such as the US, South Korea, Australia, the UK or the EU. You will influence policy in aviation, defense, sustainability, trade and innovation, advocating on behalf of Honeywell Aerospace’s broad portfolio of advanced aerospace and defense technologies. This role represents a unique opportunity to design and execute an integrated Government Relations strategy that strengthens Honeywell Aerospace’s position with policymakers and strategic stakeholders in Japan and across the region. Key Responsibilities Develop and execute Honeywell Aerospace’s government relations strategy for Japan, aligned with the company’s products, services, and overall business needs and priorities. Build and maintain strong, trusted relationships with key ministries – Ministry of Defense (MOD), Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI), and Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (MLIT) – Parliament, regulators, relevant industry bodies and key stakeholders in Japan. Advocate for policies and regulatory outcomes that support advanced manufacturing, aviation safety, defense capability, workforce skills development, and supply-chain resilience. Monitor, analyze, and proactively respond to Japanese legislative, regulatory, and policy developments affecting the aerospace and defense sectors. Support similar responses as needed across the region. Support the development and execution of Honeywell Aerospace’s government relations strategy in the broader Asia-Pacific region, supporting our business priorities and local footprint. Coordinate government engagement with broader international aerospace and defense policy priorities, working closely with global government relations and business colleagues. Serve as a strategic advisor to business leaders in the region on government affairs risks, opportunities, and stakeholder engagement strategies to support current business activities and future growth potentials and priorities. Enable and drive partnerships with major domestic aerospace and defense contractors (e.g., MHI, KHI, IHI) on joint government initiatives. Represent Honeywell Aerospace in industry forums, coalitions, and events. Drive brand recognition and excellence with key stakeholders. Responsibilities DESIRED CANDIDATE PROFILE 10-12 years of experience in government relations or policy advocacy, ideally within the aerospace, defense, or advanced technology sectors. Education: Bachelor’s degree in Political Science, International Relations, Aerospace Engineering, or a related field (Master’s/JD preferred). Deep understanding of Japanese political institutions and legislative processes, and well as good understanding of landscapes across the region. Proven expertise in policy development, contracts and budgets pertaining to the Defense Ministry and/or the Transport or Research Ministries. Experience engaging with Japanese authorities, providing insight into, shaping and responding to emerging and new legislative developments relevant to the aerospace sector. Proven ability to identify and pursue Japanese government-funded research, development grants, and defense procurement programs. Demonstrated experience influencing high‑level policy, driving advocacy strategies, and shaping regulatory outcomes. Ability to develop and execute a comprehensive government relations strategy, ensuring alignment with Honeywell Aerospace’s business objectives and working in a matrix environment. Exceptional communication, negotiation, and relationship‑building skills alongside excellent skills working independently with a strong entrepreneurial spirit. Strong networking capability, engaging effectively with officials at local and national levels. Native-level Japanese and business-level English proficiency required for cross-border stakeholder communication. Fluency or good command of other languages would be a strong advantage. OUR BUSINESS Honeywell Aerospace became a fully independent company on June 29 th , positioning itself as a global aerospace and defense leader. We total 36,000 talented employees globally. Honeywell Aerospace products and services are found on virtually every commercial, defense, and space aircraft in the world. We build aircraft engines, cockpit and cabin electronics, wireless connectivity systems, mechanical components, and navigation components. Our solutions create healthier air travel, more fuel-efficient and better-maintained aircraft, more direct and on-time flight arrivals, safer skies and airports, and more comfortable flights, along with several innovations and services that reflect exciting and emerging new transportation methods such as autonomous and supersonic flights. To learn more, please check our website here . Benefits Of Working For Honeywell Aerospace We offer a highly competitive compensation package that reflects the seniority and impact of this role, along with strong opportunities for professional growth within Honeywell Aerospace. In addition to an attractive salary, our benefits package includes a comprehensive pension and medical insurance plan. This benefits package is designed to support your well‑being, work–life balance, and long‑term career development.

review_candidates.title: Cluster Manager - Hadrian's Wall
review_candidates.description: Heritage is for everybody, and we are here for heritage.Heritage lives in places and people, memories and stories, artefacts and traditions. It can connect us all to the past, and to each other. It can make us happier, strengthen every community, and help shape society for the better. Everybody should be able to enjoy the benefits it brings.That's why, as a charity, we care for over a million objects and hundreds of historic sites in every part of England, from international icons to local treasures. And it's why we open them up, share their stories and find new ways for everybody to enjoy, learn, play and create.We're the organisation that looks after England's most important buildings and monuments, making sure our country's amazing history is available for everyone to enjoy. From world-famous prehistoric sites to grand medieval castles, Roman forts to a Cold War bunker, we bring the history of England to life.Hadrian's Wall is Britain's most impressive and most important Roman monument and a World Heritage Site, stretching for 73 miles from Wallsend in the east to the Solway Firth in the west, with its fortifications continuing down the Cumbrian coast to Ravenglass.We are looking for a site-based Cluster Manager to join our team on a permanent basis, working 36 hours per week. This is an incredible leadership opportunity for someone who is looking for the next step in their management career where you will support, develop and inspire an established management team at Carlisle Castle, Birdoswald Fort, Housesteads Fort, Chesters Fort and Corbridge Roman Town, plus the Hadrian's Wall F&B Manager and Visitor Welcome Manager.The Benefits- Salary from £39,855 - £43,087 p.a, depending on skills and experience- 25 days' holiday plus bank holidays, pro rata, rising to 28 days after 3 years- Matched pension contributions up to 10%- Flexible hours- The opportunity to progress your career within the heritage sector- Apprenticeship opportunities- Subscriptions to professional bodies- Free access to all English Heritage sites for you and up to six friends and family members- 25% discount in our shops and cafes- Enhanced maternity, paternity or shared parental leave- Options to buy additional leave- An inclusive working atmosphere everybody is supported from all backgrounds, religions and with different needs- Opportunities to go to some of our great live music and history eventsCollectively, the Wall sites welcome around 250,000 visitors a year, making it one of English Heritage's most significant sites. You will be responsible for a team of around 50 FTE staff plus volunteers and for delivering c.£2.4 million income while managing an expenditure budget of c.£1.8 million p.a. You will be expected to manage many stakeholders across the Wall and collaborate with multiple partners and local authorities along the Wall.This is an exciting time to be leading the Hadrian's Wall team, as we are developing multi-million-pound funding bids for investment at our sites along the Wall. You will be acting as the Operational Client on the Project Board, playing a critical role in the successful delivery of projects and maximising their benefits.You will manage a high-volume visitor operation, leading a dispersed team in the delivery of consistent standards and generating profit by meeting revenue targets, controlling costs and delivering a unique and memorable visitor experience. You will maintain and develop a safe and welcoming environment to support the delivery of positive, rewarding and memorable experiences for our staff, volunteers and visitors alike.You will oversee and lead your management team in the day-to-day management of their sites - providing support, direction and guidance in order that all important financial and compliance targets are met whilst also ensuring our sites are both enjoyable and inclusive places to work and visit.To be a successful Cluster Manager you will need :- to be an effective communicator with the confidence and ability to represent your sites.- to be committed to continuous personal development.- to be able to establish and cultivate effective internal and external stakeholder relationships.- to be able to develop a shared vision across a dispersed team.- to demonstrate our core behaviours of collaboration (how youwork with others), innovation (how you work through change,developing new ideas and ways of working) and empowerment (howyou make decisions and get things done)If you would like to apply, please include your CV (no more than 2 pages) and a cover letter (no more than 2 pages) highlighting how your skills and experience make you suited for the role.Interviews will be held on Thursday, 1 October in York or Newcastle.If you would like to talk to us e.g. about workplace adjustments or working patterns, please contact Andrea Selley, Operations Director - North, at andrea.selley@english-heritage.org.uk. No agencies please.Find out more about us and what we do: https://www.english-heritage.org.uk/about/ You can also meet some of our people and hear about why they enjoy working with us: https://www.english-heritage.org.uk/about/our-people/careers-with-us/Everybody's welcome at English HeritageForget the stereotypes. It takes thousands of people from every background to care for England's heritage and open it up for everybody to enjoy. We're looking for every type of person with every kind of skill and experience, and we're committed to making sure that English Heritage is an equitable, diverse and inclusive place to work. You can connect with others through our EDI networks as a member or ally. These include Ethnic Diversity, Faith & Belief, Social Equity, LGBTQ+, Neurodivergence, Age, Disability and Gender Health and Wellbeing.We take wellbeing seriously. We are committed to ensuring everyone feels safe at work and can carry out their role. To support this, we have a network of Mental Health First aiders, regular information and awareness events, unlimited access to an Employee Assistance Programme and work with our people to implement reasonable adjustments. Ofrecemos * Salario base: Q4,750.00 + Q250.00 de bonificación incentivo + Q1,200.00 de bonificación adicional. * Total mensual: Q6,200.00. * Contratación en planilla con todas las prestaciones de ley. * Horario: diferentes turnos y opciones que pueden adaptarse a su horario de estudios * Consultas médicas y crédito en farmacia con descuento. * Fondo de ahorro con tasa preferencial. * Descuentos en servicios dentales, óptica y gimnasio. * Parqueo gratuito. * Oportunidad de crecimiento profesional. * Estabilidad laboral. Interesados: enviar CV al WhatsApp 4154-4079 Correo: espana@myadviceconsulting.com
